rationale:
structural: The requirement prescribes one structural obligation. `Domain::NodeData` is an associated type with the bounds shown in the snippet: `type NodeData: Clone + Eq + Hash + Send + Sync;`. Dropping `Hash` or `Eq` would break interning and equality-as-identity. Dropping `Send` or `Sync` would break the type's thread-safety bounds. An alternative with weaker bounds would therefore violate the clause, so this is a real structural obligation.

`crates/trust-but-verify/src/domain.rs#trait[Domain]/type[NodeData]` declares exactly `type NodeData: Clone + Eq + Hash + Send + Sync;`. It carries the `{impl}` marker for `requirements.sdk.graph.NodeData`. The enclosing trait is `pub trait Domain: Clone + Send + Sync`, which matches the snippet's trait header.

The prose says two values compare equal exactly when they identify the same node. That is a semantic contract on each application's own `NodeData` type, not a structural clause of the trait. `requirements.sdk.graph.domain_types` is only cited context. It describes behavior each application domain supplies, so it adds no structural obligation here. The review root is the declaration itself, so no other root needs a marker.

behavioral: `requirements.sdk.graph.NodeData` has two parts. One is the trait-bound declaration (`Clone + Eq + Hash + Send + Sync`). The other is the semantic statement that `NodeData` values compare equal exactly when they identify the same node. The bounds are a structural, type-level choice with no independent observable behavior.

The reviewed tests also exercise the bounds. `domain_relationships_accept_opaque_types_and_send_only_errors` in `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/contracts.rs` uses a `Relationships` domain with an `Identity` NodeData and calls `check_bounds`. Its `Send` assertions need the declared bounds.

The behavioral obligation is that equal data identifies one node and unequal data identifies different nodes. Two tests cover it:
- `clones_interning_the_same_data_concurrently_get_one_handle` interns `Node(42)` from four concurrent cache clones. It asserts that all handles are equal, and that `Node(43)` gets a different handle. It asserts that `node_data` returns the right value for each handle.
- `saved_node_and_edge_inputs_survive_a_different_handle_allocation_order` shows that identity follows the data and not the handle allocation order. A fresh cache interning `Node(2)` resolves saved dependencies by data equality, and a cloned application interning `Node(1)` returns the same handle.

The first test also asserts `assert_ne!` on `node_path` for `Identity(1)` and `Identity(2)`, and equal paths for the same identity. All three tests are marked `{test}` for this requirement. I found no unmarked relevant test and no unaddressed obligation.

pub trait Domain: Clone + Send + Sync {
/// Durable identity used to intern this node.
type NodeData: Clone + Eq + Hash + Send + Sync;
Each application domain defines what identifies a node across runs. Changes to a node's contents or outgoing edges preserve its identity.
